content: The pelvis, also referred to in plural as pelves or pelvises, is the bony structure situated at the base of the spine, specifically at its caudal end. It is a component of the appendicular skeleton. Each hip bone, or os coxae, is composed of three distinct bones: the ilium, the ischium, and the pubis. The ilium represents the largest and uppermost portion of the hip bone. The ischium forms the posterior-inferior, or back-lower, section, while the pubis constitutes the anterior, or front, part of the hip bone. The two hip bones are connected anteriorly at the symphysis pubis and posteriorly to the sacrum. The pelvis also includes the socket portion of the hip joint, which accommodates the femur for each leg in bipeds or the hind leg in quadrupeds. Additionally, the pelvis serves as the skeletal girdle for the lower limbs in bipeds or the hind limbs in quadrupeds.
